messages.subject: Tuning setting of MHRM algorithm
parts:
Dear Phil,

I am dealing with a very high dimensional exploratory model and I am wondering how I can choose the optimal settings for the MHRM algorithm. Generally, for the numerical integration methods, more grid points/samples will yield more precise results at the cost of longer run time. Are there similar settings for MHRM? For example, does a higher value for MHDRAWS yield more precise results? Are their other options?

Thanks a lot in advance for your help!

Regards,
Sebastian

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Tuning setting of MHRM algorithm
parts:
Hi Sebastian,

The stochastic integration in the MHRM algorithm effectively solves the problem of numerical integration for you at the cost of slower convergence to the point MLE estimates. So long as the acceptance rates are reasonable, such as between .3-.7, then the space should be sufficiently sampled to deal with the integration problem. If not, that's when some tuning is going to be required, though more recent versions of mirt now try to calculate better candidate draw perturbation values to make this more automatic throughout the estimation. 

Of note that, with a very high-dimensional model there is a chance that the latent covariance matrix will become non-positive definite, which will result in problem and early termination. I have some plans to incorporate more robust variants for this, such as reparameterizing to use a Cholesky decomposition if the cov matrix instead, but this is lower on the TODO list since I don't believe it as flexible when specifying the model. HTH.

Phil
